topics.label: Welcome and lecture learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This opening topic introduces the course structure and sets out the learning outcomes for the lecture.

topics.label: Origins of cancer and tissue architecture
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics frame cancer as an accumulation of genetic alterations leading to a failure of normal cellular differentiation and tissue architecture, alongside experimental models for studying it.

topics.label: Benign versus malignant tumors, invasion, and nomenclature
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the defining characteristics of benign and malignant tumors, including invasion through the basement membrane, metastasis, histological progression, and naming conventions.

topics.label: Mechanisms of cancer morbidity and mortality
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic addresses the specific mechanical, physiological, and systemic processes through which primary and metastatic tumors cause illness and death in patients.

topics.label: Tumor incidence across humans and animal species
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine patterns of tumor occurrence and mortality across human populations and diverse animal taxa.

topics.label: Cancer presentation and screening strategies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the clinical presentation of tumors and evaluate the rationale, methods, and limitations of screening programs for early detection.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and practical guidance
topics.groupedBecause: This closing topic wraps up the lecture by revisiting the learning outcomes and providing directions for revision and upcoming practical sessions.
